title: Ouden OS Plan
shortDescription: Windows optimization plan for Ouden OS
description: A review-first Windows optimization playbook that stages cleanup, privacy hardening, and performance tuning through a guided wizard.
details: Ouden OS scans the current install, resolves a profile-aware plan, and packages the same decisions for wizard and ISO flows.

bulletPoints.title: Less Background Noise
bulletPoints.description: Removes preinstalled clutter and background services you do not use. Performance options are opt-in — measure them on your own system.

bulletPoints.title: Telemetry Control
bulletPoints.description: Removes the worst consumer tracking defaults without pretending every enterprise feature can disappear.

bulletPoints.title: Rollback Ready
bulletPoints.description: Keeps rollback metadata so the plan can be audited and reversed instead of acting like a blind tweak pack.

desktopQuestions.label: Optimization Level
desktopQuestions.title: How far should oudenOS go?
desktopQuestions.desc: The level decides which questions you see later. Conservative and Balanced only touch safe cleanup and privacy. Aggressive shows performance trade-offs and the optional security toggles. Expert shows everything.
desktopQuestions.note: You can come back and change this at any time.

options.title: Conservative — safe cleanup only
options.desc: Light privacy and cleanup. Nothing that changes how Windows behaves for you.

options.title: Balanced — good for most PCs
options.desc: Privacy, debloat and quality-of-life changes without real trade-offs.

options.title: Aggressive — dedicated gaming PC
options.desc: Adds performance-leaning options with trade-offs (power, memory, capture) and shows the optional security toggles. Nothing security-related is turned off unless you say so.

options.title: Expert — every option, including risky ones
options.desc: Also shows CPU-mitigation, driver-blocklist and Windows Update controls. These can reduce security, break anti-cheat, or make Windows harder to maintain.

warnings: Expert options can remove security protections and break kernel anti-cheat (Vanguard, FACEIT). Create a restore point and read each option.

desktopQuestions.label: Processor State
desktopQuestions.title: Hold the CPU at 100% minimum processor state?
desktopQuestions.desc: Sets the active power plan's minimum processor state to 100% on AC power (it does not switch plans). Do not assume a higher-performance plan is faster: on AMD Ryzen X3D CPUs Balanced is often equal or better. Benchmark Balanced vs High Performance on your own system first. Measure before/after with a frame-time capture (PresentMon or CapFrameX, several runs).
desktopQuestions.note: Raises idle power draw, heat and fan noise. Not shown on laptops.

options.title: Yes — hold the clock floor at 100%
options.desc: For users who benchmarked it and saw a benefit.

options.title: No — keep my power plan as it is
options.desc: Recommended. Balanced is a good default, especially on Ryzen X3D.

behavior.blockReason: You chose "No — keep my power plan as it is" for Processor State.

desktopQuestions.label: Fast Startup
desktopQuestions.title: Turn off Fast Startup?
desktopQuestions.desc: Fast Startup hibernates the kernel at shutdown, so drivers are not fully reinitialized. Turning it off gives a clean boot every time; cold boots get a few seconds slower.

options.title: Yes — always do a full shutdown
options.desc: Cleaner driver state after every shutdown.

behavior.blockReason: You chose "No — keep Fast Startup" for Fast Startup.

desktopQuestions.label: Hibernation
desktopQuestions.title: Turn off hibernation?
desktopQuestions.desc: Removes hiberfil.sys (often several GB) and the Hibernate option. Also turns off Fast Startup. Keep it on laptops that you hibernate.

options.title: Yes — turn off hibernation
options.desc: Frees disk space after the next restart.

behavior.blockReason: You chose "No — keep hibernation" for Hibernation.

desktopQuestions.label: Search Indexing
desktopQuestions.title: Turn off Windows Search indexing?
desktopQuestions.desc: The indexer uses background disk I/O so that searches are instant. Without it, Start menu, File Explorer and Outlook searches become much slower. Mainly worth it on HDDs.

warnings: Start menu, File Explorer and Outlook searches become much slower without the index.

behavior.blockReason: You chose "No — keep fast search" for Search Indexing.

desktopQuestions.label: Background Store Apps
desktopQuestions.title: Stop Store apps from running in the background?
desktopQuestions.desc: Uses the LetAppsRunInBackground policy (Windows 11 has no global switch). Store apps then only run while open, and their background notifications — including cloud push notifications — stop.

options.title: Yes — block background Store apps
options.desc: Phone Link, Mail, Teams and similar apps stop syncing and notifying while closed.

warnings: If File Explorer right-click menus misbehave on 24H2 after this change, revert it.

behavior.blockReason: You chose "No — allow background apps" for Background Store Apps.

desktopQuestions.label: SysMain & Prefetch
desktopQuestions.title: Turn off SysMain and Prefetch?
desktopQuestions.desc: Both preload app data using background disk I/O. They help most on HDDs, so oudenOS skips this automatically when a spinning disk is present. Expect no FPS change on SSD systems — it only removes background I/O.

options.title: Yes — SSD-only PC
options.desc: Skipped automatically if an HDD is detected.

behavior.blockReason: You chose "No — keep them" for SysMain & Prefetch.

desktopQuestions.label: Automatic Maintenance
desktopQuestions.title: Turn off Automatic Maintenance?
desktopQuestions.desc: Maintenance runs updates, scans and drive optimization when Windows thinks you are idle. If you turn it off, nothing runs SSD TRIM on schedule — you must run "Optimize Drives" yourself every few weeks.

options.title: Yes — I will maintain the PC myself
options.desc: Remember to run Optimize Drives (TRIM) manually.

warnings: Scheduled SSD TRIM stops. Run Optimize Drives manually from time to time.

behavior.blockReason: You chose "No — keep Automatic Maintenance" for Automatic Maintenance.

desktopQuestions.label: Printing
desktopQuestions.title: Do you print from this PC?
desktopQuestions.desc: If you never print, the Print Spooler and Fax services can be turned off. The spooler has a long history of security bugs (PrintNightmare).

behavior.blockReason: You chose "Yes — keep printing" for Printing.

options.title: No — turn off Print Spooler and Fax
options.desc: Printing will not work until the service is turned back on.

desktopQuestions.label: Remote Access
desktopQuestions.title: Do you use Remote Desktop or Remote Assistance?
desktopQuestions.desc: If nobody connects to this PC remotely, Remote Desktop, Remote Registry and Remote Assistance can be turned off.

behavior.blockReason: You chose "Yes — keep remote access" for Remote Access.

options.title: No — turn remote access off
options.desc: Remote Desktop and Remote Assistance stop working on this PC.

desktopQuestions.label: AutoPlay
desktopQuestions.title: Turn off AutoPlay and AutoRun?
desktopQuestions.desc: Stops Windows from opening or running anything automatically when a USB drive or disc is inserted — a common malware path.

options.title: Yes — turn off AutoPlay
options.desc: Open drives yourself from File Explorer.

behavior.blockReason: You chose "No — keep AutoPlay" for AutoPlay.

desktopQuestions.label: File System
desktopQuestions.title: Reduce NTFS bookkeeping writes?
desktopQuestions.desc: Stops NTFS writing a last-access timestamp on every read and creating legacy 8.3 short names. Small I/O savings; expect no FPS change. The third option also turns off write-cache flushing, which risks data loss on power cuts.

behavior.blockReason: You chose "No — keep defaults" for File System.
You chose "Yes — last-access and 8.3 names off" for File System.

options.title: Yes, and turn off write-cache flushing (UPS only)
options.desc: Only with a UPS or very reliable power: a power cut can lose or corrupt recent writes.

warnings: Write-cache flushing off: a power cut or hard crash can lose or corrupt recently written data.

desktopQuestions.label: Service Host Grouping
desktopQuestions.title: Group background services into fewer svchost processes?
desktopQuestions.desc: Raising the split threshold above your RAM size stops Windows from giving each service its own svchost.exe. Saves a little memory; mainly useful with 12 GB of RAM or less. It can leave Xbox controller services stuck "Starting", so it is blocked on gaming profiles.

behavior.blockReason: You chose "No — keep Windows default" for Service Host Grouping.

desktopQuestions.label: Fault Tolerant Heap
desktopQuestions.title: Turn off the Fault Tolerant Heap?
desktopQuestions.desc: FTH silently applies heap mitigations to apps that crash repeatedly. Turning it off means such apps keep crashing instead of being patched around. No performance gain is promised.

behavior.blockReason: You chose "No — keep FTH" for Fault Tolerant Heap.

desktopQuestions.label: Shutdown Speed
desktopQuestions.title: Shorten shutdown wait times?
desktopQuestions.desc: Lowers how long Windows waits for apps (3.5 s) and services (3 s) to close at shutdown. Apps that save slowly may be closed sooner; Windows still asks before ending apps with unsaved work.

behavior.blockReason: You chose "No — keep defaults" for Shutdown Speed.

desktopQuestions.label: Unused Feature Services
desktopQuestions.title: Turn off services for features this PC does not use?
desktopQuestions.desc: These services are idle on most desktops. Turning them off reduces background services; it does not change FPS.

behavior.blockReason: You chose "Keep them" for Unused Feature Services.

options.title: Wallet, smart card, media sharing, data usage
options.desc: NFC wallet, smart-card readers, Windows Media Player network sharing and the per-network data-usage counter.

behavior.blockReason: You chose "Wallet, smart card, media sharing, data usage" for Unused Feature Services.

options.title: Also Bluetooth, biometrics and Run-as
options.desc: Also turns off Bluetooth, Windows Hello fingerprint/face and "Run as different user". Only if this PC has none of these.

warnings: Bluetooth devices, Windows Hello fingerprint/face sign-in and "Run as different user" stop working.

desktopQuestions.label: Driver & Store Updates
desktopQuestions.title: Should Windows Update install drivers?
desktopQuestions.desc: Windows Update sometimes replaces a driver you installed yourself (often GPU or audio). Blocking it means you install and update drivers manually.

behavior.blockReason: You chose "Yes — let Windows manage drivers" for Driver & Store Updates.

options.title: No — I install drivers myself
options.desc: New hardware will not get drivers automatically.

behavior.blockReason: You chose "No — I install drivers myself" for Driver & Store Updates.

options.title: No drivers, and no automatic Store app updates
options.desc: Also stops Store apps updating themselves — update them manually, including security fixes.

desktopQuestions.label: Desktop Power Behaviour
desktopQuestions.title: Change desktop power behaviour?
desktopQuestions.desc: Power throttling (EcoQoS) down-clocks background threads; turning it off raises power and heat. Disabling Modern Standby switches sleep to classic S3, which some boards do not support (then sleep disappears). Desktops only. Measure before/after with a frame-time capture (PresentMon or CapFrameX, several runs).

behavior.blockReason: You chose "No — keep Windows behaviour" for Desktop Power Behaviour.

options.title: Turn off power throttling
options.desc: Background threads keep full clock. Higher power draw.

behavior.blockReason: You chose "Turn off power throttling" for Desktop Power Behaviour.

options.title: Power throttling off and Modern Standby off
options.desc: Also forces classic S3 sleep. Check that sleep still works after rebooting.

warnings: If the motherboard does not support S3, the Sleep option disappears until you revert this.

desktopQuestions.label: Telemetry Level
desktopQuestions.title: How much Microsoft telemetry should be blocked?
desktopQuestions.desc: Minimal turns off the main telemetry services and sets the lowest diagnostic level. Standard adds advertising, tips and typing/feedback data. Full also turns off telemetry tasks, speech/inking data, Insider and diagnostic services and locks down Brave's bundled extras if Brave is installed.
desktopQuestions.note: AllowTelemetry=0 is honored only on Enterprise, Education and IoT editions; Home/Pro use the lowest level they allow.

options.title: Minimal — core telemetry off
options.desc: DiagTrack and WAP push services off, lowest diagnostic level, CEIP off.

behavior.blockReason: You chose "Minimal — core telemetry off" for Telemetry Level.

options.title: Standard — also ads, tips and feedback
options.desc: Adds advertising ID, tailored experiences, online tips, typing insights, feedback prompts, the local event transcript and the PowerShell telemetry opt-out.

behavior.blockReason: You chose "Standard — also ads, tips and feedback" for Telemetry Level.

options.title: Full — every telemetry channel oudenOS knows
options.desc: Adds telemetry/diagnostic tasks, online speech, inking and contact data, app-launch tracking, app diagnostic access, online fonts, Find My Device, Insider/retail-demo/diagnostic services and Brave policies. Windows troubleshooters may not run.

warnings: Built-in Windows troubleshooters may not run while the diagnostic execution service is off.

desktopQuestions.label: Activity History
desktopQuestions.title: Stop publishing and uploading activity history?
desktopQuestions.desc: Windows records which apps and files you use and can upload it to your Microsoft account. The feed itself stays on because turning it off also breaks clipboard history.

options.title: Yes — keep activity on this PC only

behavior.blockReason: You chose "No — Windows default" for Activity History.

desktopQuestions.label: Clipboard History
desktopQuestions.title: Turn off clipboard history and clipboard sync?
desktopQuestions.desc: Win+V history and cross-device clipboard sync stop working.

behavior.blockReason: You chose "No — keep clipboard history" for Clipboard History.

desktopQuestions.label: Location
desktopQuestions.title: Turn off location services?
desktopQuestions.desc: Turns off location for Windows and apps, plus the geolocation and offline-maps services and map tasks. Automatic time zone and weather location stop working.

behavior.blockReason: You chose "No — keep location" for Location.

desktopQuestions.label: Delivery Optimization
desktopQuestions.title: Stop sharing Windows updates with other PCs?
desktopQuestions.desc: Updates are then downloaded only from Microsoft (HTTP), without peer-to-peer upload.

options.title: Yes — download from Microsoft only
options.desc: No upload of update data to other PCs.

behavior.blockReason: You chose "No — keep Delivery Optimization" for Delivery Optimization.

desktopQuestions.label: Error Reporting
desktopQuestions.title: Stop sending crash reports to Microsoft?
desktopQuestions.desc: Turns off Windows Error Reporting (policy and service) and its upload task. Crash reports can contain memory contents. You lose Microsoft's automatic problem solutions.

behavior.blockReason: You chose "No — keep error reporting" for Error Reporting.

desktopQuestions.label: Suggested Content
desktopQuestions.title: Block suggested apps, tips and promotional content?
desktopQuestions.desc: Stops Windows silently installing "suggested" apps and showing promotional content, lock-screen tips and welcome experiences.

behavior.blockReason: You chose "No — Windows default" for Suggested Content.

desktopQuestions.label: Firmware-Installed Software
desktopQuestions.title: Block software that the motherboard injects into Windows?
desktopQuestions.desc: Some motherboards use WPBT to make Windows auto-install vendor utilities (for example Armoury Crate). Blocking it also breaks firmware-based anti-theft tools if you use one.

behavior.blockReason: You chose "No — Windows default" for Firmware-Installed Software.

desktopQuestions.label: Game Mode
desktopQuestions.title: Keep Game Mode on?
desktopQuestions.desc: Game Mode is on by default. In testing it made no measurable difference either way; oudenOS only makes sure it has not been turned off. It is not a performance boost.

options.title: Leave it as it is
options.desc: oudenOS does not touch the setting.

behavior.blockReason: You chose "Leave it as it is" for Game Mode.

desktopQuestions.label: Background Recording
desktopQuestions.title: Turn off Game DVR background recording?
desktopQuestions.desc: Background recording keeps a video-encode buffer running while you play so you can save the last few minutes. Game Bar itself stays, because Windows uses it to register games. Measure before/after with a frame-time capture (PresentMon or CapFrameX, several runs).

behavior.blockReason: You chose "No — keep it" for Background Recording.

desktopQuestions.label: Fullscreen Mode
desktopQuestions.title: Make fullscreen games prefer exclusive fullscreen?
desktopQuestions.desc: Sets the system-wide fullscreen-optimization values. This is not a recommendation of which presentation mode to use: try the per-game "Disable fullscreen optimizations" checkbox first. Exclusive fullscreen also turns off Windows colour management and Auto HDR in that game. Measure before/after with a frame-time capture (PresentMon or CapFrameX, several runs).

options.title: Yes — prefer exclusive fullscreen
options.desc: A game's own compatibility setting still wins.

behavior.blockReason: You chose "No — keep Windows behaviour" for Fullscreen Mode.

desktopQuestions.label: Transparency
desktopQuestions.title: Turn off transparency effects?
desktopQuestions.desc: Cosmetic: removes blur and see-through effects. The GPU cost is tiny on modern hardware.

behavior.blockReason: You chose "No — keep transparency" for Transparency.

desktopQuestions.label: Mouse Acceleration
desktopQuestions.title: Turn off "Enhance pointer precision"?
desktopQuestions.desc: Gives a 1:1 desktop cursor. Most modern games use raw input and ignore this; it mainly affects the desktop and older games. A preference, not a performance tweak.

behavior.blockReason: You chose "No — keep it" for Mouse Acceleration.

desktopQuestions.label: Sticky Keys Shortcut
desktopQuestions.title: Turn off the Shift×5 Sticky Keys shortcut?
desktopQuestions.desc: Pressing Shift five times opens an accessibility prompt that can pull you out of a game. Sticky Keys itself stays available in Settings.

behavior.blockReason: You chose "No — keep it" for Sticky Keys Shortcut.

desktopQuestions.label: Memory Compression
desktopQuestions.title: Turn off memory compression?
desktopQuestions.desc: Compression trades a little CPU for less paging. Only consider it with plenty of RAM (32 GB+); on 16 GB or less keep it on. No repeatable gain has been measured. Measure before/after with a frame-time capture (PresentMon or CapFrameX, several runs).

behavior.blockReason: You chose "No — keep it" for Memory Compression.

desktopQuestions.label: Core Parking
desktopQuestions.title: Turn off CPU core parking?
desktopQuestions.desc: Keeps all cores unparked on AC power in the active plan. Raises idle power and heat; on many modern CPUs (especially Ryzen X3D) no gain is measurable. Measure before/after with a frame-time capture (PresentMon or CapFrameX, several runs).

behavior.blockReason: You chose "No — keep Windows behaviour" for Core Parking.

desktopQuestions.label: Boost Mode
desktopQuestions.title: Set processor boost mode to Aggressive?
desktopQuestions.desc: Changes the active plan's boost policy on AC power. Higher power and heat; results depend on the CPU. Measure before/after with a frame-time capture (PresentMon or CapFrameX, several runs).

behavior.blockReason: You chose "No — keep Windows behaviour" for Boost Mode.

desktopQuestions.label: GPU Vendor Services
desktopQuestions.title: Turn off NVIDIA/AMD background services?
desktopQuestions.desc: On NVIDIA this turns off the container services — NVIDIA Control Panel and the NVIDIA App will no longer open, and the overlay and automatic driver updates stop. On AMD it turns off Crash Defender and the UX-program launcher (FreeSync is not touched). No repeatable FPS gain has been measured.

options.title: Yes — turn them off
options.desc: Only matching vendor services are changed.

warnings: NVIDIA Control Panel / NVIDIA App will not open until the NVIDIA container services are re-enabled.

behavior.blockReason: You chose "No — keep vendor software working" for GPU Vendor Services.

desktopQuestions.label: Device Power Saving
desktopQuestions.title: Stop Windows from powering down devices to save energy?
desktopQuestions.desc: Clears "Allow the computer to turn off this device to save power" on every device. Can help with USB or network devices that drop out. Not automatically reversible, and re-plugging a device can turn it back on. Desktops only. Measure before/after with a frame-time capture (PresentMon or CapFrameX, several runs).

options.title: Yes — keep devices powered
options.desc: Undo in Device Manager if needed.

behavior.blockReason: You chose "No — Windows default" for Device Power Saving.

desktopQuestions.label: Xbox & Game Pass
desktopQuestions.title: Do you use the Xbox app, PC Game Pass or Microsoft Store games?
desktopQuestions.desc: If not, the Xbox apps and Xbox background services can go. Game Bar is kept because Windows uses it to register games. Removing them rarely changes FPS; it removes background sign-in and update noise.

options.title: Yes / not sure — keep Xbox and Game Pass working

behavior.blockReason: You chose "Yes / not sure — keep Xbox and Game Pass working" for Xbox & Game Pass.

options.title: No — remove Xbox apps and services
options.desc: Breaks Game Pass, Xbox sign-in and cloud saves. Reinstalling needs the Microsoft Store.

warnings: PC Game Pass, Xbox sign-in and cloud saves stop working.

desktopQuestions.label: Preinstalled Apps
desktopQuestions.title: Which preinstalled apps should be removed?
desktopQuestions.desc: Removing apps rarely changes FPS — it reduces background updates, notifications and Start-menu clutter. Removed apps can be reinstalled from the Microsoft Store (not available on LTSC). Apps that are not installed are skipped.

behavior.blockReason: You chose "Keep everything" for Preinstalled Apps.

options.title: Also remove optional Microsoft apps
options.desc: Also Mail & Calendar, new Outlook, Camera, Alarms & Clock, Sound Recorder, Sticky Notes, Power Automate, Phone Link (with its cross-device service), Teams, Clipchamp, Quick Assist, Dev Home, Paint 3D and more.

desktopQuestions.title: Keep Windows Search local?
desktopQuestions.desc: Removes Bing web results, search highlights and device search history from Start search, and sets the AllowCortana policy as PC-Tuning recommends.

behavior.blockReason: You chose "No — Windows default" for Search.

desktopQuestions.title: What should happen with Microsoft Edge?

behavior.blockReason: You chose "Leave Edge alone" for Microsoft Edge.

options.title: Stop preloading and default-browser prompts
options.desc: Edge stops starting at sign-in, staying in the background and nagging to be the default. Updates keep working.

behavior.blockReason: You chose "Stop preloading and default-browser prompts" for Microsoft Edge.

options.desc: Edge Update also updates WebView2, so both stop receiving security updates until you re-enable it.

behavior.blockReason: You chose "Quiet, and stop Edge auto-updates" for Microsoft Edge.

desktopQuestions.title: Remove Copilot?
desktopQuestions.desc: Removes the Copilot app (24H2+) and turns off the built-in Copilot sidebar on Windows 11 23H2 and earlier.

options.title: Yes — remove Copilot

behavior.blockReason: You chose "No — keep my taskbar" for Taskbar.

desktopQuestions.desc: Shows file extensions (so "invoice.pdf.exe" cannot hide) and opens Explorer to This PC. The power-user option also shows hidden files, hides Home and Gallery and enables long file paths.

behavior.blockReason: You chose "No — keep defaults" for File Explorer.

options.title: Show extensions, open to This PC

behavior.blockReason: You chose "Show extensions, open to This PC" for File Explorer.

options.title: Power user
options.desc: Also hidden files, no Home/Gallery and long paths.

desktopQuestions.label: End Task

desktopQuestions.desc: Lets you close a frozen app from the taskbar without opening Task Manager.

behavior.blockReason: You chose "No" for End Task.

desktopQuestions.label: LLMNR
desktopQuestions.title: Turn off LLMNR name resolution?
desktopQuestions.desc: LLMNR is a legacy local name-lookup protocol that attackers on the same network can abuse to capture password hashes. DNS and mDNS keep working; very old devices that only answer LLMNR may stop resolving by name.

behavior.blockReason: You chose "No — keep it" for LLMNR.

desktopQuestions.label: USB Selective Suspend
desktopQuestions.title: Turn off USB selective suspend?
desktopQuestions.desc: Stops Windows suspending idle USB devices in the active plan. Can help with devices that disconnect or wake slowly; uses slightly more power. Measure before/after with a frame-time capture (PresentMon or CapFrameX, several runs).

options.title: No — Windows default
options.desc: Recommended unless you have USB dropouts.

behavior.blockReason: You chose "No — Windows default" for USB Selective Suspend.

desktopQuestions.label: PCIe Power Management
desktopQuestions.title: Turn off PCIe Link State Power Management (ASPM)?
desktopQuestions.desc: Keeps PCIe links at full power in the active plan. Raises idle power; any latency effect is hardware-dependent. Desktops only. Measure before/after with a frame-time capture (PresentMon or CapFrameX, several runs).

behavior.blockReason: You chose "No — Windows default" for PCIe Power Management.

desktopQuestions.label: SmartScreen
desktopQuestions.title: Turn off SmartScreen for downloaded apps?
desktopQuestions.desc: SmartScreen checks downloaded programs against Microsoft's reputation service before they run. Turning it off removes that protection against malicious downloads. It has no measurable gaming impact.

behavior.blockReason: You chose "No — keep SmartScreen" for SmartScreen.

desktopQuestions.label: Microsoft Defender
desktopQuestions.title: Reduce Microsoft Defender?
desktopQuestions.desc: oudenOS only sets Defender policies. Defender ignores them while Tamper Protection is on (the default) — turn Tamper Protection off in Windows Security first if you really want this. Defender's services cannot be disabled by an administrator process, so oudenOS does not try. Scanning overhead shows up mostly during installs and game updates, not in-game.
desktopQuestions.note: Some anti-cheat systems may expect Defender to be running.

behavior.blockReason: You chose "Keep Defender fully on" for Microsoft Defender.

options.title: Turn off cloud lookups and sample submission
options.desc: Real-time scanning stays on; threats only cloud protection would catch may be missed.

behavior.blockReason: You chose "Turn off cloud lookups and sample submission" for Microsoft Defender.

options.title: Turn off real-time protection and scheduled scans
options.desc: Policy-level only, ignored while Tamper Protection is on. Also turns off scheduled scans and the monthly malware-removal tool. Removes real-time malware protection.

warnings: Real-time malware protection is removed (once Tamper Protection is off). Only for a PC you keep isolated from untrusted downloads.

desktopQuestions.label: Memory Integrity (HVCI)
desktopQuestions.title: Turn off Memory Integrity (Core Isolation)?
desktopQuestions.desc: Memory Integrity protects the Windows kernel from malicious or vulnerable drivers. Vanguard (Valorant, League of Legends) and FACEIT may refuse to run without HVCI, TPM 2.0 or Secure Boot. No FPS gain is promised. Measure before/after with a frame-time capture (PresentMon or CapFrameX, several runs).

behavior.blockReason: You chose "No — keep Memory Integrity" for Memory Integrity (HVCI).

options.title: Yes — turn it off
options.desc: Reversible in Windows Security > Device security > Core isolation.

warnings: Kernel protection against malicious drivers is reduced. Vanguard/FACEIT may refuse to start.

desktopQuestions.label: Virtualization-Based Security
desktopQuestions.title: Turn off VBS and Credential Guard?
desktopQuestions.desc: Requests VBS, Memory Integrity and Credential Guard off (Credential Guard is on by default on Windows 11 Enterprise). If VBS was enabled with a firmware (UEFI) lock, Windows ignores this — then disabling SVM/VT-x and IOMMU in the BIOS is the only way. Hyper-V, WSL2, Windows Sandbox and Virtual Machine Platform keep the hypervisor running. Vanguard and FACEIT may require HVCI/VBS, TPM 2.0 and Secure Boot. Measure before/after with a frame-time capture (PresentMon or CapFrameX, several runs).
desktopQuestions.note: After rebooting, check "Virtualization-based security" in System Information (msinfo32).

behavior.blockReason: You chose "No — keep VBS" for Virtualization-Based Security.

options.title: Yes — request VBS off
options.desc: Also turns Memory Integrity off. Reversible unless UEFI-locked.

warnings: Credential and kernel protection are reduced. Anti-cheat (Vanguard, FACEIT) may refuse to start. Firmware-locked VBS needs SVM/IOMMU off in the BIOS instead.

desktopQuestions.label: CPU Mitigations
desktopQuestions.title: Turn off Spectre/Meltdown mitigations?
desktopQuestions.desc: On newer CPUs this can be SLOWER, not faster. Meltdown does not affect AMD, and FACEIT requires the mitigations. Benchmark before and after and revert if it does not help. Measure before/after with a frame-time capture (PresentMon or CapFrameX, several runs).

behavior.blockReason: You chose "No — keep mitigations" for CPU Mitigations.

warnings: Exposes the system to Spectre/Meltdown-class attacks and can be slower on newer CPUs.

desktopQuestions.label: Vulnerable Driver Blocklist
desktopQuestions.title: Allow drivers on Microsoft's vulnerable-driver blocklist?
desktopQuestions.desc: Some low-level tuning tools (for example RW-Everything for XHCI interrupt tuning) need this. It also lets known-vulnerable drivers load, and anti-cheats may object.

behavior.blockReason: You chose "No — keep the blocklist" for Vulnerable Driver Blocklist.

warnings: Known-vulnerable drivers can load again.

desktopQuestions.label: Windows Update
desktopQuestions.title: How should Windows Update behave?
desktopQuestions.desc: Defer holds feature upgrades for a year; Pin stays on your current Windows version; Manual turns automatic updates off entirely. Security updates matter — with Manual you must check for them yourself.

behavior.blockReason: You chose "Leave Windows Update alone" for Windows Update.

options.title: Defer feature upgrades by a year
options.desc: Security and quality updates keep installing. No auto-restart while signed in; no early-access updates.

behavior.blockReason: You chose "Defer feature upgrades by a year" for Windows Update.

options.title: Stay on my current Windows version
options.desc: Security updates continue. Remove the pin before your version leaves support.

warnings: Feature upgrades are held until you remove the TargetReleaseVersion policy values.
behavior.blockReason: You chose "Stay on my current Windows version" for Windows Update.

options.title: Manual updates only
options.desc: Windows no longer downloads or installs updates automatically. You must check Windows Update yourself, regularly.

warnings: Security updates no longer install automatically.
